test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: After 51 litres of petrol was poured into an empty storage tank, it was still 1% empty. How much petrol (in litres, rounded off to two decimal places) must be poured into the storage tank in order to fill it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the tank is still **1% empty** after pouring 51 litres, it means the tank is **99% full**.

Therefore, 99% of total capacity = 51 litres.

To fill the remaining 1% empty space, we need to add 1% of the total capacity.

Required petrol = 51 ÷ 99 ≈ 0.51515... litres.

Total petrol in filled tank = 51 + 0.51515 = 51.52 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.52 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ff78e590b5979fec704653d306656c632eeb23591a0b919df5a73ce1111052c.png] 

Let the total capacity of the storage tank be **x litres**.

Since the tank is **1% empty**, it is filled up to 100% − 1% = **99%** of its total capacity.

⇒ 99% of x = 51

⇒ 0.99 × x = 51

⇒ x = 51 ÷ 0.99

⇒ x ≈ 51.5152 litres

⇒ Total petrol required to fill the tank completely = 51.52 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 51.52 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Representation

Any whole quantity is represented as 100%. If a part is missing by y%, then the present quantity is (100 − y)% of the total quantity.

Unitary Method for Percentages

If p% of a value is equivalent to A, then 100% of the value is calculated as (A ÷ p) × 100.</p
